sharedRules.storageConnect: Connecting storage refreshes workspace data and connection status without navigating, opening a library or expanding library menus. Preserve the current screen and close only the storage dialog on success.

popupClose.behavior: Close only the owning popup; preserve parent popup

sharedRules.newObjects: Register component type and properties, reuse existing component rules, regenerate inventory in the same change.
sharedRules.numericValues: Do not invent sizes or silently normalize existing differences. Record actual declarations and obtain approval for changed standards.
sharedRules.connectionOrder: Storage is always first in both the Connections dialog and the control-panel icon order, followed by AI, GPU and publishing connections; independent of connection state.
sharedRules.audioDraftIsolation: Every newly started unsaved story has a stable local draft ID. Audio Studio uses that ID until the story is saved; never reuse another new story’s script, cast or sounds. Earlier local drafts and legacy standalone audio remain preserved. Restoring a local story restores its own audio.
sharedRules.aiKeyEntry: OpenAI key dialog opens with an empty, initially read-only password field and focus on its heading. Pointer or keyboard focus unlocks entry and browser password-manager selection; preserve the selected key until explicit Verify & connect. Never prefill a key, connect automatically, or persist the key in browser storage. Clear on submit and close.

popupMinimize.approval: User requested universally minimizing popups to visit previous screens and connect services without losing work.
popupMinimize.control: Minimize beside Close; both use shared popup-controls.css: 26px square, 14px SVG, 2px stroke, 5px radius, identical theme accent/contrast colors and focus styles.
popupMinimize.behavior: Keep the complete dialog stack and its fields alive in this tab without close cleanup; remove modal blocking. Resume popups menu at bottom right restores the original screen, popup stack and focus. Close retains existing local dismissal semantics.
popupMinimize.persistence: Minimize is in-memory only. Explicit Save Draft persists the story preparation or source selection in browser IndexedDB, including local PDF bytes. No credential values or unrelated form fields are stored.
popupMinimize.accessibility: Native keyboard-focusable buttons, named Minimize popup; Resume popups uses a native details menu. Theme tokens, wrapped labels and viewport-constrained menu.
popupMinimize.coverage: All native Studio dialogs plus the Notifications bell popup and Ecco Desk create-ticket/task, add-member and ticket-detail overlays. Custom panels register their lifecycle with the shared Resume popups dock; controls preserve unread counts and unsent fields. Navigation flyouts and tooltips retain their existing dismissal behavior.

sharedRules.studioEntry: Tell Your Story is disabled by default, including during Google session restoration and sign-in failures. Signed-out opacity is 0.5 with a not-allowed cursor. Enable only after backend-verified Google identity is available. Entry handlers also require the current identity. Preserve button dimensions, wording, themes and explicit click to enter. Successful checks of the same signed-in identity must retain open ticket dialogs and unsent work; only an actual account change or revoked session emits the authentication-change event.
sharedRules.publishingStatus: Publishing control-panel icon shows only YouTube: Connected or YouTube: Not Connected (or the connected platform name). Hover, keyboard focus and click reveal compact theme-aware status; never open Connections from the indicator or its channel list. Connection management stays in the Connections menu.
sharedRules.popupControlAppearance: All Studio modal close/minimize controls, Activity drawer close, and Desk dialog/ticket close controls use popup-controls.css. Fixed size from the master size roster (popup-close: 30x30) border-box with no padding, margin or shadow; 14x14 SVG strokes at 2px; theme accent background and contrast foreground for default/hover/focus; focus outline uses theme text. Behaviors and popup positioning remain unchanged. Explicit flex centering, zero SVG margins and higher specificity than dialog-wide button sizing ensure icons stay centered, including Connections.
sharedRules.libraryBrowsing: Image, Audio, Video, Story and Workflow libraries use the shared compact file browser specified by libraryFileBrowser. Each opens with List selected, followed by Small icons and Large icons. Search and date/status filtering remain available. Existing actions, media players and publishing selections are preserved; metadata details appear in the file preview.
sharedRules.studioWorkspaceTabs: Audio, Image and Video use a joined Final Script / Progress / Review tab strip in the right workspace: transparent tab surfaces, square corners, theme-accent underline on active tab; native tablist/tab/tabpanel semantics, roving tabindex and Arrow/Home/End navigation. Image edits the existing prompt and previews the composed generation prompt. Video shows source speech plus selected shot directions and opens existing script/shot editors. Progress mirrors current form status without moving form-owned state; sequence controls live in Progress. Review retains existing media nodes and actions. Polling never changes the selected tab; submit opens Progress. No new generation backend or speech re-recording is implied.

notifications.appearance: Bell in GitHub/Support control panel, matching 16px icons; compact theme-aware dropdown, exact unread count in small top-right badge; hide zero badge.
notifications.behavior: Authenticated in-app feed from /api/desk/support?userNotifications=1. Show up to the five newest notices addressed to the signed-in Google subject or all users; older displaced notices are never backfilled after read/expiry. Clicking or Enter/Space acknowledges exactly one notice on the server and moves it into read history on success, reducing the unread badge; opening the bell does not mark anything read. Read receipts persist across devices, separately for each subject. Unread notices expire at the admin-set UTC deadline; Until read has no time expiry. Pending reads disable the row; failed reads retain it with a retryable error. Display severity as text and color. No private feed caching in localStorage or static files. Refresh every 30 seconds while visible and on focus/open/account changes; clear immediately and discard stale results on account change. Preserve Escape/outside/bell dismissal, header event isolation and focus return. notifications.json is no longer the active feed. Both Close and Minimize appear in the heading. Minimize retains the feed in the shared Resume popups dock; the bell also resumes it. Neither action marks notices read; account changes remove a minimized notification popup.
notifications.accessibility: Named button, aria-expanded/controls, keyboard-focusable notification rows with Read/Unread accessible names, focus retained after dismissal; textContent for feed content.

readHistory.approval: 2026-11-07: User requested Old Notfication for the last 3 read notices until expiry, numbered spaced unread entries, and No New notifications when none remain. Preserve bold unread title and body.
readHistory.appearance: 2026-11-07 user approved a three-column table: Number, Notification, Date it expires. Titles are 14px; message bodies are one size smaller at 13px. Unread rows use weight 700; read rows use 400. Numbering restarts at 1 in each section. Dates show local date and time with time-zone abbreviation; no deadline shows Until read. The existing Old Notfication bar and latest-three expiry rules remain. Expired records in administrator history use regular weight. Bell panel is 600px bounded by viewport minus 24px; fixed table columns wrap naturally with 16px vertical cell padding. Native table headers and a keyboard-operable mark-read button inside the notification cell preserve accessible semantics.
readHistory.behavior: Server returns three latest read notices per authenticated user, ordered by read time independently of the five-newest unread window. Exclude expired or withdrawn notices before limiting. Until read notices have no time expiry and stay only while among the latest three. No private history in localStorage. Expiry timer removes either kind without waiting for polling. Clear both lists on account change or rejected session. Special-offer snapshots include unread only.
readHistory.compatibility: notificationHistoryVersion 1 and readNotifications supply durable history. Older services render no invented read history.

sharedRules.settingsGitHubSync: 2026-11-07 user requested removal of Sync to GitHub from Settings. Remove its header markup, Settings mounting and unused button handler; retain the separate GitHub repository link and existing backend sync capabilities.
sharedRules.toolbarTooltipTiming: Connection and community control panels share immediate CSS hover tooltips with no animation or delay, including Discord, GitHub, Technical support and Notifications. Remove duplicate browser-native title tooltips while preserving accessible labels, unread counts, click actions and connection-status colors. Show the same tooltip on keyboard focus. Observe dynamic support/notification labels so unread descriptions stay current.
sharedRules.storyAppliedTextReview: After Apply Text auto-detection, the empty candidate panel remains display:none when hidden. User-edited character emotion supersedes AI-suggested turn defaults; explicit manual turn emotion retains precedence. Completing a voice preview refreshes Audio generation readiness immediately without enabling it over an active recording job.

activityPanel.entry: Right-edge arrow directly toggles the drawer and its accessible expanded state, without clicking a hidden inert control.
activityPanel.title: Activity, Logs and Errors
activityPanel.connectivity: Activity contains expandable credential-redacted connection checks, attempts, outcomes and issues, latest 500 retained per browser. Failures also appear in Errors with timestamp, user/session, instance, stage and detail.

Connectivity and Errors reconcile keyed existing entries, preserving open details, selected text and scroll position when new rows arrive. activityPanel.audioStatus: Preserve the exact worker progress instead of replacing it with Running Generation. Waiting for worker reconnect is shown explicitly and is never described as active synthesis.

acceleratorConnections.selection: Each card contains a RunPod instance dropdown; no instance selected by default
acceleratorConnections.status: Fresh relay health controls availability. Distinguish No heartbeat, Heartbeat lost, Service not ready and Available; do not infer RunPod power state. Visible existing help-text paragraph explains failed check.

storyJourneys.progress: Per-story browser-local last stage, script checkpoint, model settings and references; no completion inferred from navigation

storyJourneys.review: Story-filtered audio/video assets with existing approve, download and trash controls; audio script export; completed output required for guided Review

storyJourneys.sourceMedia: Localization, repurposing and ambient journeys select source assets from actual libraries

googleSignIn.entry: Google-rendered Sign in with Google button on welcome screen only. Account and Billing does not show sign-in or its loading/error messages. Existing signed-in Log off remains. No intermediate Studio popup; Google account selection only.
googleSignIn.audience: Any Google account, no domain filter
googleSignIn.verification: Server-verified Google token with one-time nonce, audience, issuer and expiry checks; identity keyed by sub
googleSignIn.authorization: Identity session cannot access shared workspace API or start GPUs
googleSignIn.session: Opaque session remains until explicit Disconnect/Log Off or server revocation. Browser-local token restored through server /me; server stores only its hash durably. Google ID tokens still require expiry/signature/audience/nonce verification at sign-in. Network outages retain credentials and never reload the app. Explicit identity disconnect does not disconnect separately authorized workspace services.
googleSignIn.dismiss: No intermediate Studio dialog. Google controls account-selection dismissal.
googleSignIn.appearance: Welcome Tell Your Story and native Google sign-in buttons have equal visible dimensions of 190px by 40px, with 16px between them. The native Google iframe transparent gutters are clipped to the button outline. Google SDK supplies unchanged logo, Google font and generic Sign in with Google text; width below 200px suppresses personalization. User menu is compact, minimum width 110px.
googleSignIn.signedInIdentity: Verified user name at far right after Education and Learning; visible dropdown arrow. Menu order: Credit and Usage, Billing, Log Off. Ribbon menu triggers share 36px height, 12px font, 10px horizontal padding and content-fit widths; user name capped at 220px; user dropdown items equal width and 40px height. Existing credit and billing actions reused. A decorative circular person icon appears immediately left of the name. The inner head and shoulders use the active theme accent; the outer ring uses theme text color. No separate keyboard stop.
googleSignIn.welcomeSignedIn: Signed in as <user name> replaces Google login after Studio verifies identity, including a restored session; Google browser session alone does not count as Studio login.

accountFlyouts.placement: Credit and Usage and Billing open to the left of the signed-in user dropdown; keep the parent dropdown open. Both also open left from the existing Account entries.
accountFlyouts.interaction: Hover opens a panel when none is open; click or ArrowLeft selects or switches the panel. Once open, pointer travel, crossing sibling rows and null focus changes never collapse or replace it. No close/X button in the slide-out. Outside click or parent dismissal closes it; keyboard focus moving outside the parent menu also closes it. Escape or ArrowRight closes only the panel and returns focus. Only one account panel is shown at a time.
accountFlyouts.content: Reuse existing credit figures, Purchase Additional Credits flow, cost figures and Refresh costs action. Without an authenticated credit adapter, a verified signed-in account shows Unavailable for its balance; a signed-out account shows Sign in to view. Sign-in never implies a balance or authorizes deductions. Real numbers require the authenticated adapter response.
accountFlyouts.appearance: Existing theme surface/text/border colors; circular person icon uses theme accent fill and theme text ring. Existing ribbon dimensions retained. Panels reveal from right to left with reduced-motion support. Purchase Additional Credits retains its resting text, background, brightness and border/shadow on hover in all six themes; keyboard focus keeps the existing visible outline.

googleSignIn.accountMenuVisibility: The separate Account and Billing ribbon dropdown is hidden, including from keyboard and accessibility navigation. Credit and Usage, Billing and Log Off remain in the signed-in user menu. The hidden legacy mount remains for compatibility with existing modules.
googleSignIn.signedOutIdentity: Rightmost header position shows the same theme-colored circular person icon with Not Logged in. Informational only, no account actions. Replaced by verified user dropdown on sign-in. Shares the compact header height (36px), 12px font and 10px horizontal padding; content-fit width.

publishingPlatforms.appearance: Six inline logo tabs; wrap on narrow screens. Background, border, text and selected accent resolve active --ecco-theme-* tokens directly, with Default fallbacks. Logos remain 18px.
publishingPlatforms.interaction: Same-window tab panels. Click, Left/Right arrows, Home/End; roving tab stop, aria-selected and linked tabpanel. Switching retains YouTube edits.
publishingPlatforms.availability: YouTube connection and confirmed uploads use the authenticated CPU storage service. Other platform connection rows and upload actions remain unavailable until their backend integration exists.
publishingPlatforms.source: Simple Icons SVG brand marks, bundled inline in publishing-platforms.js; attribution in assets/publishing/README.md.
publishingPlatforms.entry: Publish journey step opens tabs directly; no intermediate review text or Open publishing action.
publishingPlatforms.submit: One Publish button above tabs; disabled with visible explanation when no channel, destination choice or approved video is available, or selected platform is unsupported. Existing form validation and explicit upload confirmation remain required.
publishingPlatforms.youtubeAuthorization: Connections → YouTube → Connect opens Google synchronously from the user click after workspace and OAuth configuration are ready. Pending requests disable duplicate attempts. Backend-verified status updates the control panel and publishing destination selector without replacing drafts, platform selection or focus. Backend authorization, PKCE and token encryption are unchanged.
publishingPlatforms.youtubeSetup: Connections control panel owns the YouTube Connect/Connected and Disconnect controls. Connect remains enabled unless a request is in flight, and opens Set up YouTube before storage authentication when needed. The JSON file picker stays accessible; installation requires authenticated CPU setup availability. A separate Connect storage action opens a nested storage dialog and preserves the current page and selected file. Storage and Google secrets are never interchangeable. Closing a child preserves Connections and restores focus. Existing configuration discovered after storage login offers explicit Google authorization instead of replacement. No secrets are rendered or cached; bounded JSON goes only to the existing authenticated CPU endpoint.
publishingPlatforms.selection: The Publish navigation step remains active on the publishing page, using the existing theme-colored inset left highlight. Selected platform tabs use the same 3px inset left accent, replacing the bottom underline; no full accent border. Default yellow, active theme accent otherwise.
publishingPlatforms.forms: All six platforms retain editable video/title/description/visibility/audience and confirmation forms. Connection cards, Connect buttons and connection shortcuts are removed from Publishing. YouTube has a required destination dropdown populated only from authorized CPU channel metadata. Other platforms remain unavailable until backend integration exists.
publishingPlatforms.youtubeChannels: One verified YouTube channel per private workspace. Publishing shows its channel name, handle and ID. A changed destination clears confirmation; uploads verify ownership before queueing and again at worker start. Connections owns authorization and Disconnect.
publishingPlatforms.youtubeSchedule: Schedule in the existing Visibility dropdown reveals a registered date-time input using existing form styles. Browser-local time converts to UTC; backend requires a future timezone-qualified time and private upload. Other-platform forms do not expose scheduling. Completed uploads link to YouTube.
publishingPlatforms.connectionPlacementApproval: 2026-10-23: user requested the compact publishing control-panel icon and connected-platform dropdown, Connections-only management, spacing above Disconnect, multiple playlists (correcting the earlier channel request), and library-opening options inside the production-video chooser on every platform.
publishingPlatforms.controlPanel: 18px platform icon in existing 28px control slot, theme connected/disconnected colors. Click opens Connections, never uploads. When more than one authorized destination exists, adjacent dropdown lists each platform icon/channel/Connected. Unavailable or disconnected platforms are excluded. Arrow keys, Home/End, Escape, outside click and focus exit supported; Escape returns focus to trigger. No stored browser metadata is treated as authorization.
publishingPlatforms.connectionSpacing: User requested space above Disconnect in Connections; use 12px margin, matching the existing channel-label spacing.
publishingPlatforms.playlists: YouTube-only optional playlist dropdown lists every owned playlist, following API pagination. Create playlist dialog uses existing form/secondary/close styles, maximum width 540px and viewport margin 32px. Title, description, visibility (private default) and explicit confirmation; close returns focus. Create and refresh buttons use an 8px wrapping row. Loading/errors are announced; stale responses cannot change another channel. Creation and adding uploads require opt-in Enable playlists in Connections; existing upload grants remain valid. Failed playlist insertion retains the uploaded video and shows a warning, preventing a duplicate upload.
publishingPlatforms.libraryOptions: Each platform production-video chooser opens the existing Video or Audio Library in selection mode. Checkbox on every available item; Select all, Clear selection, Add selected (N), Cancel. Selections span stories, retain previews and survive library refresh/filter changes. Add selected returns to the originating platform with its draft and selected items; Cancel restores the original selection. Uploaded videos cannot be selected. Items have editable publishing titles and individual Remove buttons; shared description, visibility, audience and optional playlist apply to every selected video. Changing selection or titles clears explicit upload consent. Audio can be selected but YouTube publication explains that it requires video and remains disabled. No automatic conversion or GPU work.
publishingPlatforms.batchPublishing: Explicitly confirmed YouTube selection queues the existing authenticated single-video API once per approved video, with individual titles. Prevent concurrent submissions and re-submission of accepted or uncertain requests. Stop on a failed request, retain per-item status and direct the owner to Activity. Other platforms keep selections but uploads remain unavailable.
publishingPlatforms.pickerAppearance: Existing library cards/previews and form/button styles. Checkbox labels use 12px padding; selected-item rows wrap with 8px gap and 12px bottom margin; title labels flex with 180px minimum width. Selection controls remain keyboard accessible; empty state disables Add selected and focuses Cancel.
publishingPlatforms.publishingFeedback: User requested visible ongoing publishing and traceable Activity/Debugging/Errors. Publish shows a 16px circular theme-colored spinner, Publishing… and aria-busy during confirmed submission/queued/running work. A persistent status panel shows the last five attempts with real worker progress, timestamp, job/request ID, actual visibility and a YouTube link only after the server reports an uploaded video ID. Failures and uncertain outcomes are explicit; no synthetic progress or automatic upload retries. Completed uploads loaded from workspace records are recovered into history; reserved uploads without a known job remain unknown.
publishingPlatforms.publishingDiagnostics: Keep up to 50 credential-free attempts in this browser before calling youtube/publish, retaining returned server job IDs across navigation/reload. Activity lists all retained attempts even if submission failed before job creation. Debugging includes video/asset/channel IDs, status, progress, visibility, playlist and returned YouTube video ID; Errors records rejected/failed/unknown outcomes with redaction. Successful uploads do not create errors. Polling updates status without replacing draft fields or focus. Backend upload records remain authoritative; browser history is supplementary.

sidebarGitHub.action: Open https://github.com/ecco-ai-labs/ecco-studio in new tab with noopener noreferrer. Accessible label announces new tab.
sidebarGitHub.appearance: Same 32px button area, 16px icon, theme-aware hover/focus and glass surface as the Discord panel.

audioScriptStudio.approval: User requested character counts and optional names with later per-character voice selection, plus a real AI script popup accepting a topic or uploaded paper and single-voice/multi-turn scripts. User requested a guided Audio journey with source-only extraction, questions, suggested reusable character profiles, editable turns and Apply to main fields.

characters.location: Characters section after References; Final Script is in the right workspace.
characters.count: 1–20 active characters; character count is independent of recording length and speech-turn count.
characters.defaults: News: 1 newsreader. Podcast, Interview and Casual Conversation: Host + Guest. Other genres: 1 narrator. Genre presets apply only before user cast customization or script content.
characters.identity: Stable character IDs, independent from voice IDs. Reducing the count keeps inactive names and settings for later reuse.
characters.voices: Additional Controls contains exactly one accessible tab per active character. Each shows the selected voice with Preview, Delivery Style, Emotion, Pitch, Speed, Pause Before Speaking, optional model Expressiveness, collapsible Language and Accent, and Extra Speaking Instructions. Existing values persist when switching tabs; Left/Right/Home/End support keyboard navigation. Main screen retains compact Characters and Additional Controls sections. Explicit user voice choices remain fixed; new Chatterbox characters default to a same-language reference or Model default rather than an arbitrary cross-language sample.

modelSelection.approval: User requested adding Kokoro, VoxCPM2 and Indic Parler and mixing models per character, with a voice sample at selection.
modelSelection.placement: Character Model dropdown inside each existing Additional Controls character tab; recording model remains the default.
modelSelection.appearance: Existing dropdown, audio-voice-row, secondary speaker-icon button, native audio player and generation-dialog; no unrelated layout or theme changes.
modelSelection.behavior: Explicit character overrides survive global model changes, tab switches and AI Apply. Save per-model voice choices. Filter named voices by supported language. Each passage carries its effective model to one selected worker; sequential model groups release memory, restore script order, preserve pitch/speed/pauses and mix the soundtrack once.
modelSelection.availability: Shared model weights are separate from each machine runtime. CPU/GPU is selected at generation. Only installed and inference-verified models on that exact worker may run. No automatic accelerator fallback or GPU startup. Grey out unavailable model options and disable the selected unavailable voice/Listen controls using exact-worker capabilities. Preserve saved model and voice selections and input focus across CPU changes and health polling. Failed or disconnected health checks clear stale readiness; no automatic model substitution.
modelSelection.preview: Listen beside Voice starts a short sample for the selected model, voice, language and delivery. Native modal retains editable preview text. Saved asset IDs are reused; confirmed pending jobs resume after closing/reopening. Uncertain submissions cannot be duplicated automatically. Samples do not replace the story script or start a full recording.
modelSelection.accessibility: Native labeled selects and Listen button; existing modal Escape, Minimize, Close and parent focus; spinner/aria-busy and status for progress/errors.

scriptPopup.entry: Generate with AI on any Audio story setup or the single Audio Studio Final Script action row
scriptPopup.presentation: Native modal dialog appended to body, using generation-dialog styling, shared upper-right close button and focus return
fields: audience, genre, model-supported language, tone, purpose and source-specific questions
AI-proposed cast count, names, roles, gender, age group and personality/speaking style
saved character sets for reuse across chapters
turn count, optional spoken opening and pause
scriptPopup.uploads: Read locally, at most 20 MB and 20,000 source characters; disclose truncation. Selection replaces the source before any AI call. Read Source sends only that scope through the existing authenticated service. Never send the rest of an uploaded document, unrelated stories or chapters.
scriptPopup.review: Show editable speaker-assigned turns. Apply updates spoken script; generation never auto-starts speech. Cancel, stale state and invalid plans preserve the current script.
scriptPopup.news: Without selected scenes or source text, request current cited news through existing research service before writing narration; display cited sources in review.

audioScriptStudio.generation: Use shared audience-aware script revision and per-turn performance cues. Resolve the current character voice, language, delivery, pitch, speed and pause at Generate. Apply only model-supported controls. Uniform character settings work through existing global controls; differing pitch/speed/expressiveness require an advertised character_controls_version=1 on the selected worker. Never silently drop unsupported settings.
audioScriptStudio.limits: Existing 4,000 spoken characters, 500 characters per speech segment and 20 speech segments remain enforced before Apply and Generate.
audioScriptStudio.workflowStatus: Scheduling requires the authenticated CPU workspace audio-workflow runner; UI publication alone does not activate schedules.

guidedJourney.apply: Main page and audio draft change only on Apply. Cancel, stale source/story state and invalid plans preserve existing fields. Save and Continue with Script saves edited narration and stable character-to-turn mappings.
guidedJourney.suggestions: Adult paper podcast: normally Host + Guest. Storybook: source-specific narrator and speaking cast. News: normally one newsreader. User edits count and all properties.
guidedJourney.persistence: Explicit Save Characters stores named character sets in this browser, with stable IDs and profile properties, for reuse across chapters. Disclose browser-local storage in UI.
guidedJourney.handoff: Title, genre, audience, language, tone, narration, cast directions, source and structured script populate the main form. Save preserves manual transcript edits and seeds audio voices and turns.
guidedJourney.appearance: Existing generation-dialog, field groups, theme tokens and upper-right close control. Four text steps with current-step accent, keyboard focus and Escape dismissal.
guidedJourney.interfaceLanguage: English for menus, clarification questions, source reviews, cast explanations and character-property descriptions, independently of the selected script language. Spoken content retains the selected language and native script; preserve source quotations and character proper names. All AI enhancement requests explicitly keep user-facing questions and notes in English.
guidedJourney.progress: Use the existing generation-spinner (16px, currentColor, existing reduced-motion behavior) in the primary action with Generating Script…, disabled duplicate submission and aria-busy. Preserve the current step and character edits while waiting. AI follow-up questions appear in Script Clarifications on the current Characters step, preserving earlier answers. Only a valid script advances to review; failures stop the spinner and allow retry in place.

languageStyle.placement: Questions before Generate Script, plus the main Audio setup. Custom shows a required free-text direction.
languageStyle.behavior: All UI labels stay English. The choice guides vocabulary and sentence complexity in the selected spoken language. Everyday Hindi requests common spoken words and short natural sentences, avoiding highly Sanskritized Hindi, difficult literary Urdu and literal translation. The selected style and custom instructions survive Apply, save, reopen and next-chapter handoff.

audience.placement: Audience dropdown on the main Audio setup and Questions step; genre comes first in Questions.
audience.behavior: Options change with genre. Keep choices valid for the new genre; clear incompatible choices and ask for selection. Preserve legacy saved audiences as labeled saved options when reopening. Apply, saved drafts and AI requests retain the chosen category. English labels, existing dropdown styling and native keyboard behavior.

guidedJourney.sourceSelection: Shared source-picker uses three equal-width, equal-height desktop panes: full Document Preview, yellow-bordered Selected Text, and a dedicated Improve with AI pane. The AI pane has one compact horizontal control ribbon above the prompt: Story Type, Genre, Audience, Language and a 30px sparkle AI action with an accessible Improve with AI name and tooltip. Remove the visible Prompt label and selected-text helper sentence. Story workspace choices carry over from Story Details and synchronize immediately both ways; requests combine those defaults with the prompt. Native dropdowns use existing options and show full values on focus/hover; the ribbon remains one row with horizontal overflow within the settings strip on narrow panes. Preserve equal pane geometry. Settings changes invalidate pending or unapplied AI output, including restored drafts, while retaining source, selected text and prompt. Prompt and AI Output textareas have identical heights in the same grid. Use AI Text copies output into Selected Text; Clear AI Output removes only that output. AI questions and errors use nested accessible popups, never the output area; Clarifications show recommendation text and 2–4 concrete answer buttons from AI notes, one marked Recommended. Clicking a choice immediately resumes selected-only improvement with that approved answer; no repeated blocking clarification loop after approval. Continue Anyway opens the validated current draft for review without another request, while Edit Prompt focuses the prompt. Missing choice metadata falls back to preserving source details. Real failures show actionable recovery advice, Try Again and Continue Without AI, which focuses Apply Text without applying. Source, settings and prompt changes invalidate decisions. Original selection remains unchanged until Use AI Text, and final Apply Text remains explicit. Hide the redundant For: caption. Selected Text starts empty on a new PDF/TXT/Markdown upload; only explicit highlighting, page/chapter selection or manual edits add content. The bottom ribbon spans all three panes and contains Select Pages, Select Chapter, Find and Replace, optional Save Draft, Clear Text and Apply Text. Clear Text is a normal secondary button immediately left of Apply Text. Page/chapter/replace tools open upward in bounded panels, one at a time; Back, Escape and outside pointer dismiss only that tool and preserve work. Successful page/chapter selection closes its tool and focuses Selected Text. AI sends only highlighted words within Selected Text or all its contents, never unselected document content. The uploaded document remains unchanged. Reject stale AI replies and retain text on errors or cancellation. Distinct excerpts append in selection order with blank lines; deduplicate repeated highlight events and enforce caller limits. Find and Replace uses exact literal matches in the caret line or all selected text. Only final Apply commits source content. Save Draft retains the source, selected text, prompt and uncommitted AI output locally. Story Details choices are visible in the AI ribbon; Story workspace Apply first checks selected source compatibility with the current title, type, genre and brief. A clear mismatch or uncertain assessment requires explicit Use Anyway; an unavailable check requires Use Without Checking and never implies a verified match. Choose Different Text preserves the source picker. Story or selection changes invalidate assessments and confirmations. New uploads reset prompt and results; parent close cancels nested confirmation. On narrow screens the three equal-size panes stack in order and the ribbon wraps. Use existing themes, independent content scrolling and the resizable shared dialog.

bookends.placement: Optional Opening and Closing textareas in Questions, with English example placeholders; replace the separate Opening Title choice in Characters.
bookends.behavior: Blank fields omit the corresponding spoken section. Accept wording or directions such as a welcome or moral; AI adapts them to the selected script language and style. Opening uses the existing opening field; Closing occupies the final script segment, within existing character/turn limits. Review shows editable Opening and Closing labels; added body turns go before Closing. Apply, save, Audio Studio and reopening retain the directions and spoken output. No new backend schema or speech runtime is required.

guidedJourney.saveProgress: All Story setup saves use the existing generation-spinner and Saving Story… inside the submit button, aria-busy and duplicate-submit protection. Preserve the busy label through Audio setup observers. On failure restore the prior idle label and retain the draft. Acknowledge creation before progressing; update the story list from that confirmed response. Do not wait for an unrelated full workspace refresh: normal background polling handles it.
guidedJourney.editorialReview: Generate Script first drafts then refines for audience, idiomatic spoken language, listening rhythm and character interplay. Storybook defaults allocate multiple narrative beats. The second request receives only selected source plus the draft; it adds bounded English delivery cues outside spoken words. Source facts, plot, selected chapter boundaries, cast identities and bookends remain fixed. Existing drafts change only on Apply. Spinners remain active through both requests and stale results are rejected.
guidedJourney.chapterSelection: Main Upload and Audio Upload share PDF Pages and Chapter selection in the same source-picker. Select Pages extracts only physical PDF page ranges locally. Find Chapter with AI uses a bounded numbered outline, then verifies every candidate chapter page plus neighboring boundary pages; exact page/line/text anchors bound local extraction, excluding the next chapter. Never use contents entries or fall back to page 1/full book. Ambiguity, invalid anchors and oversize sources fail without selecting/truncating. Show chapter title and PDF page range for review; explicit Apply alone commits the selected text. Narrative AI gets only the applied excerpts; locator AI may inspect the book outline, every candidate chapter page and neighboring boundary pages to find it. New uploads are pending until a selection is applied, preventing stale-source reuse.
guidedJourney.tone: Tone uses Natural, Warm, Conversational, Playful, Dramatic, Calm, Professional, Informative, Suspenseful, Inspirational and Custom. Preserve custom saved instructions; no unrelated field or style changes.
guidedJourney.chapterFeedback: Show missing input/connection errors and per-page reading/AI-boundary progress beside Chapter controls. Large book indexes omit repeated headers/footers and prioritize heading candidates; exact boundary verification remains mandatory.
guidedJourney.scriptReview: Selected-text Improve with AI is available while reviewing character turns before Apply. Repeated improvement operates on the current suggested replacement, preserving the original exact replacement range. Storybook generation suggests uniquely named sound cues after script refinement; errors preserve the script and remain visible for retry.

drafts.controls: Save Draft on every preparation step and source selection; Resume Saved Draft in Generate with AI and Resume Saved Selection in main Upload.
drafts.content: Source file, selected excerpts, scope and pending-selection state; instructions, audience, language, tone, questions, answers, cast, edited script, sound cues, current step and script version.
drafts.scope: Explicit browser-local save keyed by story/local-draft identity and entry surface. Parent story remains in Story Library as a local draft. Resume is explicit and does not apply or generate.
drafts.feedback: Saving Draft spinner, confirmed saved time, readable failure with current work retained. AI/storage not required for saving.
drafts.connections: Show missing workspace storage/AI before Read Source and Continue. Open Connections minimizes this preparation; returning refreshes the connection notice. Submission failures are focused and scrolled into view.

guidedJourney.turnPlanning: Keep the existing editable Number of Turns proposal. On generation count mismatch, preserve the valid draft and pause with requested/actual counts, Review Generated Draft, and Continue with N turns. The creator may instead edit Number of Turns and regenerate. Do not silently accept or discard the candidate. Failed retries preserve it; source/brief/cast changes block stale acceptance. Save Draft restores the pending decision. Validate character coverage and runtime limits independently of count. Failed editorial refinement retains valid dialogue for a targeted retry.

finalScriptReview.placement: Right-hand Audio workspace contains Final Script, Progress and Review tabs. Final Script supports manual editing, Generate with AI and selected-text Improve with AI; Named cue attachments remain inline; global Music & Effects moves to Additional Controls. Progress shows actual service state with a spinner, not invented percentages. Review shows only the newly generated recording. Reuse the existing responsive two-column grid, theme tokens and character-tab styles. Native tab roles, arrow/Home/End navigation; no automatic tab switching on polling.
finalScriptReview.selection: Select a word, sentence or paragraph. Improve with AI opens a native generation-dialog with instructions above a read-only Selected Text area, followed by editable Suggested Replacement and Apply. Send only the selected passage and explicit instruction, no whole script, PDF or saved story.
finalScriptReview.apply: Snapshot story, text and selection. Apply replaces exactly that range, retains all surrounding words and character assignments, rejects stale state and enforces existing limits. Editing invalidates old delivery cues. Do not regenerate or modify an existing audio file; clearly state regeneration is needed.
finalScriptReview.accessibility: English labels, native modal focus, shared upper-right Close, Escape and focus return; visible spinner/aria-busy during requests.
finalScriptReview.generationDirections: User requested audience, genre and narration style in generation. Show a Generation Directions summary before numbered turns, with the stored audience, genre, tone, narration/language style and per-character delivery. Carry a bounded structured performance_brief to the audio worker and saved asset; native text-directed engines incorporate it separately from speech. Other engines use only supported controls; reviewed Chatterbox acting cues map to expressiveness with explicit user settings taking precedence. Include the brief in delivery-refinement and preview-cache identity. Source/PDF text is never part of this performance metadata.

soundDesign.approval: User requested narrative sound effects and scene background music, including a Jinn arrival and Mediterranean-inspired desert music. On 25 October the user requested automatic missing-sound generation, one-stop cue review beside numbered turns, unchanged AI text editing, a worker-count progress bar, and Spoken script moved to Final Script.
soundDesign.placement: Final Script contains one compact Generate with AI / Improve with AI action row and numbered editable turns, with no duplicate Spoken script overview or Generation Directions summary. Each turn has Add Sound and collapsible cue review with name/type, description, Audio Library, preview/upload/generation and collapsed settings/timing. Music & Effects and Edit turns and opening remain available in Additional Controls. Save as Workflow sits inside collapsed References. Direction metadata still reaches generation unchanged.
controls: Unique Sound Name, Generate Sound, Sound Model, Duration, Compute
Audio Library selection, Upload Audio and Preview Sound
Start at Passage, optional exact After These Words trigger, End after Passage for beds
Volume in dB, Fade In / Out, Soften during speech, Loop for beds
Add Sound Cue, remove cue, Apply
soundDesign.appearance: Reuse form, section-head, fieldset, generation-filter-row, workspace-label-option, secondary buttons, shared generation-dialog and theme tokens. English interface, spinner and aria-busy, native Escape and focus return; uploads remain nested and preserve the parent.
soundDesign.planning: AI plans uniquely named sound cues from the final spoken script, audience and direction; excludes unselected PDF content. Plans survive Story Apply, durable save and Audio handoff. Generate audio creates missing assets serially before submitting speech/mix; enabled empty plans first request AI cue suggestions. Disabled sound design never creates audio. Existing assignments are preserved. Script edits invalidate timing until reviewed. Cancel and stale requests cannot overwrite current edits.
soundDesign.timing: Cue passages use exact spoken chunks; a unique trigger phrase splits synthesis immediately after those words. Timing comes from actual post-speed/pitch PCM boundaries. Preserve voice settings, zero extra pauses between split chunks, retain the existing 80-segment limit and invalidate cue timing after script edits.
soundDesign.mixing: Worker uses CPU FFmpeg to layer authenticated Audio Library snapshots over speech, with explicit gain, fades, looping for beds and optional sidechain compression during speech. Effects play once up to 30 seconds. Result is one stereo WAV. No external URLs, implicit asset choices, synthetic placeholder sounds .
soundDesign.activation: Frontend and coordinator require sound_design_version=1 on every live worker of the selected compute class. Unsupported services fail clearly instead of dropping tracks. UI publication alone does not activate mixing.
soundDesign.scheduling: Individual recordings only in this release. A workflow containing enabled sound cues is rejected rather than reusing old cue positions on a newly generated script.
soundDesign.generation: Per-cue Generate Sound uses MOSS SoundEffect v2 for effects/ambience and ACE-Step 1.5 for instrumental music. Description, duration and explicit CPU/A100/B200 selection; CPU default; no fallback. Queue through authenticated storage; show real progress; attach only a durably saved asset from Audio Library. Generated assets remain reusable. Capability is advertised only after runtime qualification; source/UI deployment alone is not readiness. Completing a cue refreshes Audio Library choices without rebuilding sibling cue controls, preserving their pending state, polling and eventual exact-cue attachment. Missing sounds use the main selected compute without fallback; CPU remains default. Persist confirmed job IDs and completed assets in a browser journal; resume polling after refresh or network failure, retry only confirmed failed jobs, and block duplicate submission when the response is uncertain. Late results enter Audio Library but cannot overwrite changed scripts/cues. Each successful assignment saves immediately. Inline edits use existing controls/theme, preserve focus/open cue panels, and do not alter Generate with AI or exact-range Improve with AI. Grey out unqualified sound models and disable Generate Sound on that exact selected worker, with a reason. Audio Library and Upload remain enabled. Inline sound creation follows changes to the main Compute selection; existing cue edits and focused controls are retained. Keep availability feedback separate from live job progress and errors.

audioScriptStudio.storyPersistence: Save the reviewed audio preparation, character identities/properties, source selection, script and named sound plan in the authenticated story record. Restore that record when a local draft is absent. Save and Continue opens Audio directly for prepared audio stories.

speechProgress.approval: User requested a progress bar followed by Generating Speech: 1 of 14 passages complete.
speechProgress.source: Only validated completed/total counts from real worker progress; no elapsed-time estimates.
speechProgress.appearance: Native progress with shared accent, full panel width, status text below. Existing spinner covers sound preparation, queued work and mixing.
speechProgress.states: Determinate for valid passage counts; indeterminate while waiting for first worker count; separate status for mixing, failure and saved recording.
speechProgress.accessibility: Named progress element and polite status text.

audioWorkflowScheduling.approval: User requested automatic generation of news, podcasts and storybooks for the weekend goal.
audioWorkflowScheduling.activation: Authenticated workspace capability required. Saving pauses the schedule; Enable Schedule is explicit. Run Now does not disable an existing schedule.
audioWorkflowScheduling.persistence: Definitions and run history belong to the existing CPU workspace service. Browser drafts are not running schedules.
audioWorkflowScheduling.recovery: Stable run and audio job IDs prevent duplicate audio after restart. Interrupted AI calls pause without paid automatic retry.
audioWorkflowScheduling.availability: Selected compute only; no fallback or provisioning. Controls stay unavailable until storage connects and the updated runner is advertised.
audioWorkflowScheduling.deletion: Pause persisted audio schedules successfully before moving them to this browser Trash.
audioWorkflowScheduling.scope: Automatic audio generation and saving; publishing is separate. Existing layout, themes and model controls are reused.

eccoDesk.appearance: 2026-11-08 user requested restoration of the previous Desk UI, retaining only Ecco AI Labs name and the actual Ecco logo. Restore navy #112a38 sidebar, original #f3d463 yellow selection/accent, #f7f8fa page background, white cards/forms, original Arial typography, font sizes, spacing and primary navy controls. Existing logo-transparent.png appears at 46px with the Ecco AI Labs wordmark and Ecco Desk sublabel on loading, sign-in and navigation. Standalone Desk is light; embedded support retains the pre-redesign theme-aware heading/sign-in exception and original light ticket surfaces. This supersedes the all-purple Desk restyle. Functional notification tabs, creation controls, history and the Studio bell table remain.
eccoDesk.layout: Support uses a headset with microphone beside Discord/GitHub, inside the existing 32px asset-icon button with a 16px glyph. Support renders in the main page with Back to Studio. No team-workspace link appears on the customer surface. Desk retains its metric cards, scrollable table, right detail drawer and centered dialogs.
eccoDesk.content: Ecco Desk branding; internal tasks, customer support, personal assignments, explicit team access, activity history. Customer support shows only the requester’s support tickets.
eccoDesk.states: Loading, signed out, empty, error, filtered empty, populated, busy, open dialog/drawer. Errors use role=alert and success uses role=status; network requests time out. Refresh rechecks server permissions.
eccoDesk.interaction: Header Support opens inside Studio without needing storage/GPU access. Existing Google sign-in is reused on welcome with a return intent. Esc dismisses the current Desk dialog/drawer; focus is trapped and returned, including within Shadow DOM. Tab order follows the visible content. No nested Desk dialogs.
eccoDesk.accessibility: Support icon has an accessible name. Forms have labels, constraints and inline errors. Dialog/drawer have named dialog roles and aria-modal. Icon-only actions are named; decorative SVG icons are hidden. Reduced motion supported.
eccoDesk.authorization: Server verifies existing opaque Google session. Identity is keyed by Google sub. Customers cannot see other tickets, internal notes, staff directory or staff audit data. Roles never come from email/domain. First administrator explicitly activates using existing workspace access plus verified identity; later grants refer to an existing verified account. No email invitations are sent. Studio uses /api/desk/support: every request uses requester permissions even for staff/admin identities; lists, details, replies and history are limited to the authenticated Google subject. The endpoint never returns members, internal notes, team activity or setup controls, and rejects team operations. Separately authorized team operations remain on /api/desk. Account changes clear cached tickets and discard responses for the previous identity.
eccoDesk.storage: Existing CPU storage API and SQLite on persistent Ecco volume. Dedicated desk_* tables are excluded from legacy workspace records. No tickets, tokens or access keys are stored in GitHub Pages/source. Separate ChatGPT login is not used.
eccoDesk.build: Run npm ci && npm run build in desk/. Checked-in desk-app.mjs is the generated browser bundle; authored TSX/CSS are included in the inventory.

conversations.approval: User requested email replies in ticket history, switching to queued live support, agent acceptance and 7 AM–11:59 PM Pacific support hours.
conversations.appearance: Reuse existing Desk colors, controls, drawer and conversation layout. Email, chat and ticket replies carry source labels; internal notes retain their separate styling.
conversations.layout: Online support controls sit inside each support ticket drawer. Team navigation adds Live support with a queue and availability checkbox; team administrators can connect the support inbox in Team members.
conversations.interaction: Customer explicitly joins/leaves the queue; staff explicitly enables availability and accepts the next waiting customer. One live chat per agent. Polling preserves the reply draft and current focus. Closing the detail panel stops customer presence refresh. Customers can Close issue or Reopen issue on their own tickets. Closing keeps history, ends any queue/live chat, and disables Online support until reopened. Support staff retain their existing status controls.
conversations.accessibility: Status changes use role=status, errors use role=alert; checkbox has an accessible label; all chat actions are buttons with disabled states. Existing dialog focus trap and Escape dismissal apply.
conversations.authorization: Server enforces requester ownership on customer endpoints, active staff role and assigned-agent rights on chat actions, FIFO acceptance, presence expiry and America/Los_Angeles 07:00 inclusive through 23:59, closing at midnight. Every transcript is attached to its existing ticket. Only administrators can start support-inbox OAuth.
conversations.email: Reply headers and a random ticket reply address establish thread identity. Authenticated active agents can accept, reply, delegate, resolve, close or reopen from the mailbox; commands are private action events with an agent-only acknowledgement. First agent reply accepts an unowned case. Another agent must receive an explicit delegation before replying. Customer and staff thread references stay separate; subjects alone never authorize a ticket.
conversations.hours: Live chat only: 7 AM–11:59 PM Pacific daily, including automatic PST/PDT changes. Opening new tickets and sending ticket/email replies remain available 24/7.
conversations.ownership: Accept case or Accept chat assigns one responsible agent. Only that agent sends public replies or resolves/closes the issue. The owner or an administrator can explicitly delegate to an active agent. Accepted cases cannot be unassigned. Delegating live chat queues it until the delegate accepts; transcripts stay on the same ticket.
conversations.nativeSupport: Support email includes Accept, Resolve, Close, Delegate and Reopen compose actions. Sending the action email confirms it; authenticated commands never enter the customer transcript or get forwarded. Normal agent replies use the ticket reply address and forward only to its opener. Native Google Chat cards use verified app callbacks and exact Google member identities; activation requires an owner-configured interactive Chat app and approved support space.
conversations.staffSignIn: Standalone team Desk uses a separate persistent staff session and its own Google account chooser. It never reuses, replaces or logs out the Studio customer session. Embedded customer support continues to use Studio identity and requester-only permissions.

composer.approval: User requested a permanently visible typing box for customers and support personnel, with animated dots while the other participant types.
composer.layout: Reply form is a non-scrolling sibling of the flexing ticket transcript. Drawer scroll area has min-height:0 and overflow:auto. Composer keeps existing 26px desktop / 21px narrow inset, 3-row textarea bounded to 18dvh, and a reserved 18px typing-status line.
composer.focus: Focus the composer after opening a loaded ticket when permitted; preserve caret and drafts across polling, and return focus after send or send failure without stealing it from another control. Preserve newly typed text while an earlier message is sending.
composer.scroll: Open at latest messages; follow new messages only when already near the bottom, or after sending. Reading older messages preserves scroll position. History and properties remain available in the scroll area; composer stays visible on Conversation.
composer.presence: Live participants only: boolean typing pulses every 2 seconds while actively editing public chat. Stop on 4 seconds idle, blur, hidden tab, send, clear, internal-note mode, ticket close or unmount. Server expires presence after 8 seconds and clears it on send, end, delegation or lost agent presence; no draft text is transmitted.
composer.feedback: Named opponent is typing with three animated dots above the textbox. Polite accessible status, stable height, inherited Desk colors, reduced-motion fallback. Receiving chat state refreshes every 1.5 seconds; unrelated staff cannot see typing presence.

responseNotifications.approval: User requested replies only to the ticket opener, exact ticket association for multiple tickets from the same user, and a very small support-response badge over the headset.
responseNotifications.appearance: 12px badge positioned at the headset button’s upper-right, 8px white count on the theme error color with a 2px contrasting ring; 9+ cap, hidden for zero. Unread customer ticket rows have a pale yellow background, a 3px left accent and a compact Support replied badge. The conversation tab shows New reply. Existing header button dimensions and icon stay unchanged.
responseNotifications.content: Support has responded on N tickets in the tooltip and accessible button name.
responseNotifications.interaction: Poll the authenticated customer-only notification endpoint every 10 seconds while visible, and after reading. Read receipts are per requester and ticket, acknowledge only when the latest support reply end is visible inside the ticket drawer in the focused browser tab. Opening or polling a ticket does not acknowledge off-screen replies. Reading updates that ticket and the headset badge immediately; never clear another ticket or a newer unseen reply. Hidden/history/background views do not mark replies read.
responseNotifications.authorization: Only own public support responses count; customer messages, private notes and other customers never appear. Logout/account changes discard stale responses.
responseNotifications.email: Each email is bound by original message headers or its unique ticket reply address. Accepted staff replies are relayed only to that ticket’s opener, without CC/BCC. Native mailbox commands are acknowledged only to the agent; legacy direct-to-customer Sent copies are logged without duplicate delivery.

ticketTypes.approval: User requested a Type dropdown for Bug, Feature Request, Task and related requests.
ticketTypes.content: Type: Bug, Feature Request, Task, Question, Other. New support defaults to Bug; internal tasks default to Task. Existing support tickets remain Other.
ticketTypes.appearance: Reuse existing form-grid, labels and native selects; no new colors or dimensions.
ticketTypes.interaction: Persist requestType independently of support/internal permissions and Category. Display in ticket summaries and details; authorized staff can update it with existing Save changes.
ticketTypes.accessibility: Label-associated native select with existing keyboard focus and modal tab order.

userNotifications.approval: User requested a User Notification tab with all-user or specific-user delivery, informational/warning/error severity and read-or-admin-duration lifetime.
userNotifications.appearance: Reuse existing Desk sidebar, light ticket sections, form-grid, native inputs, primary/secondary actions, history table and error/status styles. New form padding 22px (16px mobile), 20px section gap, 11px labels, 12px controls, 5px control radius, 10px/11px control padding. Severity text uses existing informational blue, warning brown and error red treatments. Bell keeps original dimensions and theme colors.
userNotifications.content: Notifications; All users / Specific user; Informational / Warning / Error; title (160 chars), message (4000 chars); Read or duration ends (3 days default, whole 1–365 days) / Until read; Publish notification, Clear form; history with recipients, severity, status, dates, read count and Withdraw. The left navigation entry is always visible in standalone Ticketing Studio; accounts without administrator access receive a clear permission explanation.
userNotifications.states: Loading, unavailable old service, empty history, active, read (targeted recipient), expired, withdrawn, saving, failure retains draft and success resets form. History lists latest 200 notifications.
userNotifications.interaction: Only administrators can open management. Native recipient selector uses verified Studio identities with name/email; target is stored as stable subject. History details disclose full message. Reading moves a notice from unread into the last-three read history until expiry.
userNotifications.accessibility: Label-wrapped native form controls, browser required/min/max validation, aria-busy saving, role=alert errors, role=status success, visible keyboard focus, native details/summary and table headers. Responsive form stacks at 650px; wide history scrolls within its section.
userNotifications.authorization: Server enforces an active Desk admin role or verified active direct membership of the privately configured Google group for notification management and mutations. Group capability grants no staff role, ticket access or team-management permission. Membership is bound to the authenticated Google subject, cached for at most 60 seconds on reads and checked fresh before publish/withdraw; provider failures deny the group grant. Customer support route denies management even for admin identities. Feed and receipts use only authenticated subject; no audience IDs or directory leak to customers. A minimized popup keeps its original story identity; its Cancel never targets a newly selected story.
generationCancellation.accessibility: Native type=button; contextual accessible name Cancel audio generation or Stop image/video generation, keyboard activation and existing focus styles. Mirror cancellation controls share the same real job state; closing a popup never cancels implicitly.

Existing generation guards remain authoritative; verification is optional.

productionReleases.approval: User approved GitHub-only development/testing and an administrator Releases screen for reviewing a collection of changes, preparing a release, previewing it, explicitly publishing to the website and rolling back.
productionReleases.identity: desk/src/Releases.tsx in the existing Ecco Desk right-hand page. Reuse panel, table, heading, button, link, badge, input, help-text and status types. Rocket navigation icon.
productionReleases.appearance: Reuse existing Desk typography, surfaces, borders, tables and primary/secondary actions. Release toolbar and rows wrap with 12px gaps; panels have 20px separation. Release summaries and notices use 16px/20px padding. Forms use 20px padding and stack below 650px. Release-name input uses 10px/12px padding, 1px theme border and 6px corners. Theme accent for success and focus; no additional popups or hover Back controls.
productionReleases.content: Current production, Pending changes, Release name, Prepare release, Prepared releases, Preview, Publish to Production, Release history and Prepare rollback. Statuses distinguish prepared, queued, publishing, published, failed and uncertain receipts.
productionReleases.behavior: Prepare pins a complete source SHA and successful main push build run. Publish sends the prepared release identifier; subsequent development changes never replace its source. Failed/missing tests disable preparation. Setup blockers, an active publication and a changed production baseline disable publishing. Rollback prepares a previously published tested build and still requires Publish.
productionReleases.authorization: Only existing verified Desk admin roles. Staff, customers, notification-group-only admins and the personal support endpoint have no release access. Release credentials stay in a private backend file; Cloudflare credentials stay in GitHub production environment secrets.
productionReleases.accessibility: Named native buttons, labelled input and tables, heading focus after preparation, alerts for errors and polite status for receipts. Persistent reading position; refresh does not replace input state. Mobile tables scroll internally. Existing theme-accent page Back is retained.
productionReleases.persistence: Server SQLite stores prepared releases and durable dispatch intents, scoped to administrators. GitHub production receipts and Cloudflare canonical deployment establish publication, not the HTTP dispatch response. No release credentials or history in browser storage.
productionReleases.limits: Frontend publication only; backend code, database migrations and GPU model deployment stay separate. GitHub immutable previews retain 10 verified builds; artifacts retain 90 days. Production remains disabled until hosting, domain, OAuth, API origins and release credentials are configured.

pdfTextSelectionIntegrity.verification: source-picker.test.cjs and UPLOAD-08 real PDF mouse selection.

completeChapterAudio.approval: User requested removing the 4,000-character/80-turn restrictions and automatic complete speaker-labelled script conversion on Apply Text.
completeChapterAudio.behavior: Preserve full selected scripts and every turn. Generate Script assigns all source words to named speakers in bounded analysis sections. Review and Apply retain user edits; older applied prose drafts repair missing speaker assignment before Generate. Audio synthesis uses bounded batches and assembles one recording, with worker capability checks.

generatedScriptReview.identity: story-script-review.js; story-script-dialog variant; shared character renderer in story-workspace.js.
generatedScriptReview.appearance: Existing theme typography/surface/border/accent/error. 1400px within 96vw and 94vh. Two-column 2:1 grid, 20px gap, right minimum 280px; 12px internal gaps. Header and Apply footer remain visible while turn/property panes scroll. Textarea minimum 84px. Below 700px columns stack within one scrollable content pane. No horizontal viewport overflow.
generatedScriptReview.content: Generated Script, Script, numbered editable turns, speaker selectors, Characters, Character properties for, Apply Text. Voice/delivery for audio; voice/delivery/appearance for video.
generatedScriptReview.states: Loading section counts, retryable AI/connection failure, editable success, invalid empty turn/duplicate character validation, stale story protection.
generatedScriptReview.interaction: Native modal with shared Close and Minimize. Closing keeps a per-story Resume Script draft; minimizing keeps live state. Character edits update speaker names. Apply alone commits; Generate remains on main page. Closing source/review never starts media generation.
generatedScriptReview.accessibility: Named regions, labelled native selects and textareas, heading focus after generation, keyboard-selectable cast, polite progress and alert error. Focus returns to Generate after Apply or Resume Script after close.
generatedScriptReview.persistence: Selection and reviewed turns/properties autosave in the current story draft. Reopen resumes edits without regenerating. Failed generation preserves the selection; older applied content stays unchanged until Apply.

compactTypography.approval: 2026-11-08: User requested every font reduced by 2 points and corresponding box/dropdown adjustments. This supersedes earlier typography and padding numbers throughout the contract.
compactTypography.fontSize: Every authored nonzero UI font size uses calc(original - 2pt): exactly 2.6667 CSS pixels. Apply once at its declaration, preserving inherited text and responsive clamp values. Studio body starts at calc(16px - 2pt); embedded/standalone Desk body and host start at calc(14px - 2pt). Zero sizes used for icon-only labels stay zero.
compactTypography.layout: UI padding and gaps of at least 6px decrease by 2px per edge/gap. Fixed text line heights decrease 2px; standard compact text buttons are 28px high, Story Details inputs/dropdown triggers 40px, output tiles 52px, Next 44px. Two-line story brief is 54px. Equal Story/Audience card dimensions and viewport-bounded dropdown panels remain. At widths below 700px, Credit and Usage opens within its account menu rather than outside the left viewport edge; credit rows wrap and the panel scrolls vertically. The account menu is horizontally clamped within 12px viewport margins on mobile, including content and viewport changes.
compactTypography.exceptions: Google-hosted sign-in iframe typography and imported PDF canvas/text-layer fonts remain provider/document controlled. Media dimensions, glyph icons, popup close/minimize 26px targets and toolbar icon-only targets remain unchanged.
compactTypography.verification: Browser checks cover exact font reductions, inherited/dynamic text, Desk shadow DOM, theme changes, keyboard focus, content fit and no horizontal overflow at 1440x1000 and 390x844; existing workflow suite remains required.
compactTypography.supersededBy: sizeRoster: element sizes now come from the master size roster; the calc(original - 2pt) rule remains only for properties the roster does not set.

sizeRoster.approval: 2026-11-08: User approved one size per element type through a 24-screen audit, two rounds of before/after mockups and per-row decisions; user requested a master roster that new screens follow, with new element kinds added to it, editable in Studio Look and Feel and applied to the whole UI by administrators. 2026-11-08 later: user approved a named size scale with every element assigned a size name, a live side panel and Pick on page.
sizeRoster.source: design-system/size-roster.json (repository default). design-system/sizes.css is generated from it by node scripts/size_roster.mjs and never edited by hand.
sizeRoster.runtime: design-system/sizes.js compiles the roster into one stylesheet in every Studio and Desk page, including Desk shadow roots, after all page styles. Roster rules share one specificity above page rules; when an element matches several roster entries the later entry wins (types, then variants).
sizeRoster.publishing: Studio > User Preferences > Look and Feel opens a side panel beside the live screen (Elements on this screen, Sizes, Pick on page). Changes preview instantly; administrators (Desk admins or the approved administrator group) Apply to everyone, publishing a numbered version to /api/look-and-feel.Only administrators (service-confirmed or listed in design-system/look-and-feel-admins.json) see Look and Feel; a Colors tab edits theme colors (LOOK-04). Use repository default publishes a reset.
sizeRoster.newElements: An element whose type exists in the roster takes that type's size and must not set its own. A new kind of element is added to the roster (a type, or a variant of a type) in the same change, with its contract component. ROSTER-01 fails on any visible element whose size is neither its roster type's size nor inherited.
sizeRoster.keptCurrent: Entries marked keptCurrent keep their pre-roster sizes by the user's choice and remain editable.
sizeRoster.verification: node scripts/size_roster.mjs --check; qa ROSTER-01, ROSTER-02, LOOK-01..03; backend/test_ecco_look_and_feel.py.
sizeRoster.scale: Sizes are named and grouped (Title, Heading, Text, Control height, Icon, Image). Elements refer to a size by "@id"; a scale change updates every element using it. Compiled as --ecco-size-* custom properties.
